[Package]
Name="labview_open_source_lib_epoch_datetime"
Version="1.2.0.6"
Release=""
ID=254ceec1a20b434d39cef6e7665c0c35
File Format="vip"
Format Version="2017"
Display Name="Epoch Date & Time"


[Description]
Description="Epoch Date & Time is a unified time library for LabVIEW\0D\0A\0D\0AThis library provides support for UTC, Unix and GPS Epochs, enabling the conversion of timestamps into the proper frame of reference. It supports leap seconds to accurately convert from UTC (coordinatad universal time) to GPS (global positioning system) with proper offset based on divergence between UTC and TAI (international atomic time). It is completed with an extensible interface for Date-String formatters and comes pre-loaded with ISO8601 and RFC5322 support.\0D\0A\0D\0A- ISO8601 is the international standard for date and time on almost every modern interoperable systems and databases. (RFC3339 strings can be read with non-strict ISO validation flag)\0D\0A- RFC5322 is the standard for email headers format, which includes a Date-Time string. This library covers only the date-time string part of the standard.\0D\0A\0D\0AEpochs\0D\0AUTC epoch starts on 1904-01-01\0D\0ALocal System is referenced to UTC with a time offset (from -14:00 to +12:00)\0D\0AUnix epoch starts on 1970-01-01\0D\0AGPS epoch starts on 1980-01-06\0D\0A\0D\0AKeywords: \0D\0ALeap Year, leap second\0D\0AUTC Time zone offset\0D\0AISO8601, RFC5322, Epoch\0D\0AGPS, Unix, UTC, Local System Time\0D\0A\0D\0AExample:\0D\0ATaking the following date and time: January 1st, 2021 @ 11:50:22.587 in Montreal:\0D\0A\0D\0AUTC DateTime = 2021-01-09T16:50:22.587Z\0D\0ANon UTC DateTime = 2021-01-08T11:50:22.587-05:00\0D\0AISO Date = 2021-01-09 or 20210109\0D\0AISO Calendar month = 2021-01\0D\0AISO Week = 2021-W01\0D\0AISO Week-Day = 2021-W01-6\0D\0AISO Ordinal Date = 2021-009\0D\0AThe reverse operation (ISO8601 DateString to Timestamp) supports all the above accepted formats, validates the input string for compliance and returns the ISO Format type matched.\0D\0A\0D\0ARFC3339 Format\0D\0ARFC3339 is based on ISO8601 but allows for a few deviations. A notable one is the space to replace the "T" in the UTC DateTime. Instead of providing an entirely separate method, the DateTime to Timestamp exposes a "Strict ISO?" terminal which can be set to false to accept RFC3339 format as a valid date-time string.\0D\0A\0ARFC5322 Format\0ANeeded for HTTP1.1 Support. Allows backward compatibility with RFC850 and ANSI-C time formats.\0A\0D\0ACompare Timestamps\0D\0ABecause of the high resolution of the LabVIEW Timestamps, and the limited resolution of date-time strings, validation of equality needs to be performed with a certain precision. A practical method has been added to the palette to compare with a pre-defined resolution. The node defaults to 1 millisecond, but can be set to any fractional of multiple of 1, and units available span from nanoseconds to weeks. For simplicity, months and years have been ommitted because of extra computation required to handle leap years and different month lengths. All comparisons are performed in timestamp epoch (UTC).\0D\0A\0D\0AGPS, TAI and UTC\0D\0AGPS clocks and International Atomic Time are continuous and evenly-spaced, whereas UTC compensates for the fluctuation of Earth's rotation to keep the "year" synchronized for human activities. Therefore, leap seconds are sometimes added or removed to UTC time. Based on the history of the number of leap seconds added to the UTC, one must use this look-up table to make the exact time conversions. Leap Seconds record is kept in a table maintained by an international consortium (https://www.ietf.org/timezones/data/leap-seconds.list)\0D\0A"

[Package]
Name = "jki_lib_state_machine"

ID =61c59a1e50c5584e59f41ac35a8f3eef
File Format = "vip"
Format Version = "2017"
Display Name = "JKI State Machine"

[Description]
Description = "The JKI State Machine� is a template you can use for quickly creating your own LabVIEW applications. This is the very same template that is used by the JKI team, nearly every day, and is the result of years of refinement by our team of LabVIEW experts. We encourage you to post any questions or comments to the JKI Software Forums. There you will find an active community of JKI software users, as well as JKI team members.\0A\0AHow to use:\0A\0AFind the JKI State Machine in the palettes\0A1) Functions >> JKI Toolkits >> JKI State Machine\0A\0AUse QuickDrop to place a JKI State Machine on the block diagram\0A1)  Press Control+Space then type "JKI"\0A2) choose the "JKI State Machine" option that appears\0A\0ALaunch the JKI State Machine Explorer by either\0D\0AA) Right-click on a State String, Case Structure, or Event Structure to launch JKI SM Editor\0D\0AB) Press Control+Space then Control+J when you're on the block diagram of a VI containing a JKI SM\0A\0D\0D\0AUsing the Right-click menu on the JKI SM Parts for increased productivity:\0D\0A- Select an item in the tree to make that frame visible\0D\0A- Click back and forward to navigate the history\0D\0A- Drag and drop frames to reorganize the order\0D\0A- Right-click on items in the tree-view to rename, duplicate, delete, etc.\0D\0A- Right-click on a state string and choose Goto State Frame to jump to that frame of the JKI SM.\0A- Right click on a state string or frame and choose Find Callers to find all callers of a state\0A- Right-click on a bundle or unbundle by name and choose Find Data Accessors to find all accessors of the data.\0D\0A\0D\0ASpecial thanks to Jim Carmody for open sourcing his CaseSelect tool as a launching off point for the JKI SM Editor."
Summary = "JKI State Machine"
License = "BSD"
Copyright = "Copyright (C) 2005-2018, JKI"
Distribution = ""
Vendor = "JKI"
URL = "http://jki.net/state-machine/"
Packager = "JKI"
Demo = "FALSE"
Release Notes = "- Now includes the JKI State Machine Editor (JKI SM Explorer window and LabVIEW right-click menu integration)\0A- Changed While Loop Label to JKI State Machine (2018)\0A- New Icons and Color Scheme, designed for the future!\0A- Major performance improvements to Support VIs ("Parse State Queue", "Add State(s) to Queue", and "Build State String with Arguments")\0A- Support VIs are now configured for "Inline SubVIs into Calling VIs" and "Subroutine" priority to reduce memory footprint and execution time\0A- Replaced deprecated FP.Open property with FP.State\0A- Added new arguments to "UI: Front Panel State" (Open, Standard, Close, Closed, Hidden, Hide, Maximize, Maximized, Minimize, Minimized)\0A- Special thanks to @mcduff14 and @drjdpowell for their performance improvement ideas and feedback on this thread https://github.com/JKISoftware/JKI-State-Machine/pull/3\0A\0AFixes\0A- Fixed Issue #9 (JKI SM Explorer VI keeps running when target VI FP is closed)\0A- Fixed Issue #10 (Editor Plug-ins that call "Term:Data Type" (as Variant) need a Request Deallocation to avoid LV crash)\0A- Fixed Issue with Find Data Accessors not always working well (failing to open and consuming CPU)\0A- Fixed Issue (SM Editor #79) where SM Explorer window does not disappear occasionally\0A- Fixed Issue (SM Editor #86) Can't open JKI SM Explorer for multiple JKI SM's on same BD\0A- Fixed Issue (SM Editor #89) Find Callers does not work on Idle, Event Structure frame\0A- Fixed Issue #13 Right-click menu item 'Insert "Add State(s) to Queue"' fails"
